provenance.note: Generated by drivers/survival on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.3.3. This is a TARGETED FOLLOW-UP to the v4.3.2 red-team. 4.3.3 is a purely ADDITIVE release: it closes finding C5 by exposing DiscreteTimeSolution.converged / .n_iter (matching CoxSolution/GLMSolution per Amendment A3) and adds a summary() convergence line; the IRLS is untouched. Consequences validated here: (1) R8 -- all discrete_time numbers are BIT-IDENTICAL 4.3.2->4.3.3 (drift 0), confirmed by re-running the CPU correctness at 4.3.3; (2) C5 -- a new convergence-diagnostics study validates the .converged/.n_iter flag against R glm's own convergence behaviour (matches bit-for-bit incl. iteration count, no false-positive). The correctness, default-degeneracy (R15), MPS precision, MPS fp32 boundary (R13), and Cox CPU scaling studies are RE-RUN FRESH at 4.3.3 (Mac) and reproduce v4.3.2. The expensive CPU monthly-scale studies (scaling/breakdown/R-choke) and ALL Forge CUDA studies are CARRIED FORWARD from v4.3.2 (generated at 4.3.2; bit-identical since the IRLS is untouched, re-verified by the fresh 4.3.3 CPU correctness check) rather than re-run, as the additive flag cannot change them. Torch 2.12.1; the MPS solver envelope is version-sensitive while the host float64 acceptance gate is the version-independent fail-loud guarantee (R14). Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2); forge (NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti CUDA, carried forward).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/survival-v4.3.2.md. 4.3.3 adds only the convergence diagnostics (C5 RESOLVED); no validated number changes (R8 drift 0). The new convergence-diagnostics study is the one piece of genuinely new evidence.

r.engine: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph; glm(binomial) for discrete-time

reference.name: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph
reference.what: The R survival package (Therneau): survfit() for Kaplan-Meier, survdiff() for the log-rank test, coxph() for proportional hazards. Discrete-time survival is validated against R glm(family=binomial) on the identical person-period design pystatistics builds internally -- on the small survival::lung design, the large real survival::flchain design, and (RIGOR R15) the every-unique-event-time design the intervals=None default constructs.

studies.title: Correctness vs R survival -- Powerhouse (CPU / fp64), per quantity
Discrete-time CPU vs R on real flchain (~83k person-period rows), per quantity
Convergence diagnostics .converged / .n_iter vs R -- Powerhouse (CPU) (C5)
studies.note: 4.3.3 closes C5 by exposing DiscreteTimeSolution.converged / .n_iter. The new flag is validated against R glm(binomial)'s OWN convergence determination on the identical person-period design (R9/G3). Both .converged AND .n_iter match R bit-for-bit across well-posed, default, separation-extreme, perfectly-separated-covariate, and all-censored designs: the separated covariate reports converged=True at 18 iterations exactly as R (R also converges on separated data at a large finite coefficient -- not a false positive), and the all-censored degenerate design reports converged=False at the 25-iteration cap, matching R. No false-positive convergence claim.

studies.title: Default invocation discrete_time(intervals=None) vs R -- behaviour match (RIGOR R15)
Wall-clock vs R on survival::lung -- Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Per-fit median over timed repeats. With the 4.2.0 O(n log n) Cox PH, all four procedures are within a small constant factor of R on the tiny lung dataset; the scaling studies below carry the asymptotic and at-scale claims. Unchanged at 4.3.2.

studies.title: Cox PH CPU scaling vs R -- Powerhouse (CPU / fp64) (priority 3: CPU never lags R)
studies.note: Synthetic proportional-hazards DGP. pystatistics Cox PH is O(n log n) (vectorized reverse-cumsum risk sets + a Fenwick-tree concordance), matching R's complexity: the pystatistics/R wall ratio is FLAT at ~1-2.6x across n=250..8000. Re-run fresh at 4.3.3; reproduces v4.2.4/4.3.2.

studies.title: fp32 GPU no-silent-wrong boundary on discrete-time's regime -- Powerhouse (MPS) (R13/R12)
studies.note: RIGOR R13: the regression R12 fp32 gate is re-proven on discrete-time's OWN person-period regime (heavy low-weight interval-dummy block, near-separation, large coefficients, conditioning) plus a real flchain-quarterly anchor, on the MPS gated-CG path. Every accepted float32 fit reached the float64 optimum (deviance to the fp32 tier); refusals are fail-loud true-positives / conservative refusals that force=True recovers (cond >= 2e5); NO accepted-but-wrong band. Per R9/G3 a reference-degeneracy guard excludes designs whose fp64 reference is itself undefined (a uniformly-deep baseline yields zero events) rather than judging fp32 against a meaningless optimum.

studies.title: fp32 GPU inference-SE no-understatement on discrete-time's regime -- Powerhouse (MPS) (R13/R12)
studies.note: The R12 proof extended to the INFERENCE outputs (the covariate SEs the user reads). On every accepted float32 fit the covariate SEs track the fp64 CPU fit to the Tier-2 contract (rtol <= 1e-2) and no covariate SE is understated -- instability surfaces in the SE exactly as in R. The float32 discrete-time path never returns a covariate that is wrong AND looks precise.

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling -- Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: GPU value proposition (priority 4: the GPU must EARN its existence by beating the CPU in its regime). Wall-clock of the binomial GLM fit on the person-period design (expansion excluded). The MPS float32 inner solve is a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient (squaring-free); MPS converges across the whole flchain sweep including quarterly and monthly, and wins materially over the CPU at scale. Reproduces v4.2.4 at 4.3.2. CARRIED FORWARD from v4.3.2: this evidence was generated at pystatistics 4.3.2; the 4.3.3 change is purely additive (convergence diagnostics .converged/.n_iter) and leaves the IRLS untouched, so these numbers are bit-identical -- re-verified by the fresh 4.3.3 CPU correctness run (discrete_time drift 0).

studies.title: Discrete-time float32 acceptance boundary on real flchain -- Powerhouse (MPS)
studies.note: Per flchain bin granularity: the MPS float32 fit is accepted across the sweep (coef_max_rel ~3e-6..6e-5 vs CPU fp64). The host float64 Newton-decrement gate is unchanged, so an accepted fit is genuinely at the float32 tier; a float32-infeasible design would fail loud (-> backend='cpu'). faithfulness_rel ~0 confirms the fit-isolated measurement reproduces the public discrete_time coefficients. Re-run fresh at 4.3.3; reproduces v4.2.4/4.3.2.

studies.note: The person-period expansion is a pure-Python double loop but a small fraction of end-to-end at scale (~1.7% at monthly); the GLM fit dominates, which is why the GPU speedup is reported on the fit. studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling -- Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA gpu_fp64 (exact)
studies.note: The robust large-scale path: CUDA gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-13) and accepted at every granularity including monthly -- materially faster than the same-host CPU fp64 fit (~28x at monthly). Priority 4: the GPU earns its existence at scale. The CPU baseline is this throwaway CUDA-venv's numpy/BLAS (monthly ~77s) and is slower than the frozen v4.2.4 forge CPU (~38s, a different BLAS build); the speedup is a fair WITHIN-ENV CPU-vs-CUDA comparison and the GPU-wins conclusion is robust to the baseline (even against the faster 38s CPU, gpu_fp64 at ~2.7s is ~14x). CARRIED FORWARD from v4.3.2: this evidence was generated at pystatistics 4.3.2; the 4.3.3 change is purely additive (convergence diagnostics .converged/.n_iter) and leaves the IRLS untouched, so these numbers are bit-identical -- re-verified by the fresh 4.3.3 CPU correctness run (discrete_time drift 0).

studies.note: CUDA float32 converges across the whole sweep including monthly and wins large over the CPU (~50x at monthly); exact fits at every scale use gpu_fp64 (above). As in the fp64 study, the CPU baseline is this throwaway venv's numpy/BLAS (slower than the frozen forge CPU); the within-env GPU-vs-CPU speedup is fair and the GPU-wins conclusion holds against either baseline. record_fields.max_abs: max absolute difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements
record_fields.max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements (correctness headline)
record_fields.n_elements: number of scalar elements compared for that quantity (1 for scalars, vector length otherwise)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.ratio_pystat_over_r: pystatistics wall-clock / R wall-clock at a given n (flat across n once both are O(n log n))
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference of the float32 GPU covariate coefficients vs the CPU fp64 fit (float32 tier ~1e-5 when accepted)
record_fields.forced_max_rel: RIGOR R9: max relative error of the REJECTED float32 fit if forced (large -> the fit is genuinely wrong -> the rejection is a correct fail-loud)
record_fields.faithfulness_rel: max relative difference between regression.fit on the reconstructed person-period design and the public discrete_time coefficients (~0 -> the fit-isolated measurement is faithful)
record_fields.expansion_frac_of_e2e: person-period expansion time / end-to-end discrete_time time (small at scale -> the GLM fit dominates)
record_fields.cov_coef_max_rel_vs_r: R15: max relative difference of the DEFAULT invocation's covariate coefficients vs R glm on the identical every-unique-event-time design (~1e-15 -> the default matches R)
record_fields.baseline_hazard_max: R15: the largest per-interval baseline hazard under the default binning (reaches 1.0 only in the no-censoring separation extreme, matching R)
record_fields.accepted_dev_rel_vs_fp64: R13/R12: deviance of an ACCEPTED float32 fit vs the fp64 reference (<= fp32 tier -> the right optimum; a large value would be a silent-wrong fit)
record_fields.forced_dev_rel_vs_fp64: R13/R12: deviance of a REFUSED fit when FORCED, vs fp64 (large/non-finite -> the refusal was a correct true-positive)
record_fields.se_rel_gpu_vs_cpu: R13/R12 inference: max relative gap of the accepted float32 covariate SEs vs the fp64 CPU SEs (<= Tier-2 1e-2; never understated)
record_fields.classification: R13/R12 boundary verdict: safe / refused-true-positive / refused-force-recovers / ref-degenerate (excluded) / SILENT-WRONG
record_fields.inference_verdict: R13/R12 inference verdict: inference-warned / refused (fail-loud) / INFERENCE-SILENT-WRONG
record_fields.py_converged: C5: the new DiscreteTimeSolution.converged flag (4.3.3) vs R glm's converged
